items.title: Unitree shares end first month on the STAR Market about 240% above issue price, roughly 53% below the first-day high
items.summary: Unitree Robotics (688836) closed at 514.98 yuan on Sept 18, against an issue price of 150.80 yuan and a first-day intraday high of 1,100 yuan on Aug 19. Market capitalisation was 208.3 billion yuan on Sept 18 versus 444.9 billion yuan on the first day. The listing priced at about 219 times earnings; Q1 2026 revenue rose 68.49% year on year while net profit excluding one-offs fell 52.55%.
items.why_it_matters: The first listed pure-play humanoid maker is the public-market price signal for China's humanoid sector, and its valuation now reflects a limited float rather than earnings.

items.title: IFR counts about 7,000 humanoid robots sold worldwide in 2025, many to research and data-collection buyers
items.summary: The International Federation of Robotics tallied humanoid sales for the first time, at about 7,000 units for industrial and professional service use in 2025. IFR said many were bought for research, testing and AI data collection rather than continuous productive work, and that automotive pilots typically involve small numbers of robots. For scale, 542,000 conventional industrial robots were installed in 2024. Reported by Reuters; the IFR release itself was not opened.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first standards-body unit count for humanoids and sits well below vendor shipment claims, which matters for judging real deployment in the US and China.
items.note_definition: IFR definition: human-like appearance and autonomous operation in environments designed for people; legs not required; excludes consumer and military humanoids.

items.title: AgiBot and Chimelong deploy 300+ robots at Zhuhai theme park; 20,000th AgiBot robot delivered
items.summary: AgiBot and Chimelong Group launched the first phase of a deployment at Chimelong Spaceship Park in Zhuhai with more than 300 robots across seven scenarios, including performances, guided tours, retail stations and hotel services. The launch coincided with delivery of the 20,000th robot off AgiBot's production line. The release gives no model-by-model fleet breakdown, autonomy measures or commercial terms.
items.why_it_matters: It is a large single-site fleet and a cumulative production count from the volume leader among Chinese humanoid makers, though the use case is entertainment rather than industrial work.

items.title: H1 2026 humanoid shipments above 22,000 units, with five Chinese makers at 86% (Counterpoint)
items.summary: Counterpoint Research put global humanoid shipments in the first half of 2026 at more than 22,000 units, up nearly 300% year on year. AgiBot led with about 9,700 units (43%), followed by Unitree at over 7,000 (31%), then Galbot, UBTech and Leju, with Chinese firms taking the top five places and 86% of units. Counterpoint published on Aug 20; Robotics & Automation News re-reported the AgiBot claim on Sept 18. Counterpoint projects more than 50,000 units for full-year 2026. Per-company figures for UBTech differ across outlets and are omitted.
items.why_it_matters: Read next to the IFR 2025 count, it shows Chinese vendors supplying most humanoid units, which is the volume side of the US-China comparison.
items.note_dedup: Counterpoint release predates window (Aug 20); check whether already recorded before adding.

items.title: Qualcomm to acquire PickNik, steward of the MoveIt open-source manipulation framework
items.summary: Qualcomm Technologies agreed to acquire PickNik, which maintains MoveIt and sells the commercial MoveIt Pro platform. No price or closing date was disclosed and the deal is subject to customary conditions. Qualcomm said it will integrate MoveIt with its Dragonwing robotics platform while keeping MoveIt open source and hardware-agnostic. Announcement dated Sept 22 (ROSCon) by The Robot Report; Evertiq carried it Sept 24.
items.why_it_matters: A US chip vendor is buying control of the most widely used open motion-planning stack, tying a common robotics software layer to its own silicon.
items.note_source: Qualcomm page body could not be loaded; facts taken from Evertiq copy of the release.

items.title: Skild AI publishes S1 self-play result: 140+ simulated years, policy transferred to a humanoid playing soccer
items.summary: Skild AI's blog describes its S1 robotics foundation model trained through more than 140 years of simulated self-play in NVIDIA Isaac Sim on soccer tasks, then transferred to a real humanoid that plays against people. Skild says S1 is otherwise limited to human-level ability because it is pre-trained on human data. Results are self-reported, with no independent benchmark.
items.why_it_matters: It is a US foundation-model developer claiming sim-to-real transfer of a learned multi-agent policy, a capability area where US labs currently publish more than Chinese hardware vendors.

items.title: XPeng holds IRON supplier conference after opening dedicated humanoid line; mass production targeted for end of 2026
items.summary: XPeng held a supplier conference on Sept 22 and said it signed supplier designation agreements and is scheduling production for its IRON humanoid. The Guangzhou line, opened Sept 8, has more than 80% of core processes automated. XPeng targets mass production by end of 2026 with initial deployment in its own stores and campuses and deliveries in China and overseas in 2027. Volumes, suppliers and contract values were not disclosed; the 'world first' claim is XPeng's own.
items.why_it_matters: A Chinese carmaker is moving a humanoid onto an automotive-style production line ahead of Tesla's Optimus line, which has no announced output yet.

items.title: Toyota reportedly estimates a need for about 400,000 factory robots from 2028, around 1 trillion yen a year
items.summary: According to Reuters as summarised by AI News, Toyota discussed with investors an estimated need for about 400,000 robots, humanoid and non-humanoid, covering Toyota, group companies and major suppliers, with spending of about 1 trillion yen (about $6.4 billion) a year from 2028. Toyota has not confirmed the full investment or its duration. The Reuters original was not opened; Seoul Economic Daily gives a 150,000 (Toyota) / 250,000 (affiliates) split but calls all of them humanoids, which the AI News summary does not.
items.why_it_matters: If confirmed, it is the largest single-customer robot demand figure reported for a non-Chinese manufacturer, and most of it would be non-humanoid automation.

items.title: Apptronik CEO says US lacks a gear supply base; actuators can be up to 60% of a humanoid's bill of materials
items.summary: Speaking on Fox Business on Sept 22, Apptronik CEO Jeff Cardenas said the US has major shortages in items such as gears and that actuators can be up to 60% of a robot's bill of materials. He said Apptronik has developed more than 80 electric actuators, and that the US leads in AI while China has the stronger industrial robot manufacturing base. Statements are the CEO's own and were taken from a secondary summary.
items.why_it_matters: A US humanoid maker names actuator and gear sourcing as the constraint, which is the hardware side of the US-China gap.

items.title: Mach Industries adds $600M at a $3.7B valuation for autonomous aircraft, strike and counter-drone systems
items.summary: Mach Industries raised $600 million, extending its June Series C, at a valuation of $3.7 billion, up from $1.8 billion in June. The company makes autonomous aircraft, long-range strike systems and counter-drone weapons and is moving from prototyping to scaled manufacturing at a 115,000 square foot site in Huntington Beach, California. Lead investors were not named in the source.
items.why_it_matters: Defense autonomy is drawing physical-AI capital at a pace comparable to humanoids, and US procurement rules are pushing that demand toward US-built systems.

items.title: FY2027 NDAA: House Sec. 163 bars DoD from Chinese humanoid robotic systems; Senate bill has a parallel UGV ban; conference pending
items.summary: The House-passed FY2027 NDAA (H.R. 8800, passed 216-212 on July 22) Sec. 163 bars DoD from procuring, leasing or obtaining covered humanoid robotic systems made in China or using Chinese firmware, software, AI models, cloud services or remote access. The SASC-reported Senate bill (S. 4784) has Sec. 5813 barring DoD from covered unmanned ground vehicles, including humanoids, from Chinese-controlled firms, and Sec. 847 widening drone-component restrictions to batteries, motors and controllers. Which text survives conference is undecided. Law-firm review dated Sept 9.
items.why_it_matters: It is the main pending statutory route to exclude Chinese humanoids and robot components from US defense purchasing, alongside the FCC Covered List action.
items.note_dedup: House passage was July; Senate section numbers come from the law-firm summary.

items.title: China reportedly tightens scrutiny of humanoid-robot IPOs to curb valuations
items.summary: Digitimes, citing The Information, reports Chinese regulators are tightening review of humanoid robotics listings to separate commercially viable firms from a crowded field. The regulator, rules and affected companies were not identified in the accessible text, and the underlying report is paywalled. Context: AgiBot started a Hong Kong IPO process in July, and Leju and DEEP Robotics have listing applications accepted.
items.why_it_matters: A slower listing pipeline would affect how quickly Chinese humanoid makers can fund production capacity.

items.title: UBTech begins first consumer deliveries of UWORLD U1 humanoid against 13,361 prepaid orders
items.summary: UBTech said deliveries of the full-size UWORLD U1 companion humanoid to households began Sept 16. The company reported 13,361 orders at its June 30 launch; prices run from 119,800 yuan (U1 Lite) up to 990,000 yuan for top variants. The robot is sold for companionship, not chores, and is not available to US buyers. Delivery count so far was not disclosed.
items.why_it_matters: It is one of the first full-size humanoids sold to households through a retail channel, in China only, ahead of any US equivalent.
items.note_source: Pandaily page body could not be loaded; delivery date and order count come from search summaries and June launch coverage.

items.title: Feather raises $7.6M pre-seed, launches $30,000 wheeled humanoid platform for developers
items.summary: Feather, founded in 2025 by Hoa Mai and Parsa Bakhtiari, raised a $7.6 million pre-seed led by Gradient Ventures. It sells a modular robot for software developers at $30,000 and says it has passed $1 million in revenue, with robots working as restaurant cooks and lab cleaners. Revenue is company-reported.
items.why_it_matters: A US developer-platform bet that robot software will separate from hardware, as it did in phones.

items.title: GENISOM AI (智身科技) closes Series B of several hundred million yuan led by UAE's Stone Venture
items.summary: Beijing embodied-AI robot maker GENISOM AI announced a Series B of several hundred million yuan led by Stone Venture (UAE), with Hongshan Capital, Guangdong Finance and others participating. The company makes robots for power, petrochemical, firefighting, security and emergency use and says it had produced over 15,000 units cumulatively as of June 2026. The exact amount and the unit count are not independently confirmed.
items.why_it_matters: A Gulf investor leading a Chinese robot round is a capital-flow data point, and the company sells special-duty robots rather than general humanoids.

items.title: PitPro's tire-changing robot goes live at a Kal Tire shop in Calgary
items.summary: San Francisco startup PitPro Automation put its first commercial tire-changing system into a Kal Tire location in Calgary, Alberta. The system changes four tires in under 15 minutes using two oven-sized robots and is built to fit existing service bays. Funding was not disclosed.
items.why_it_matters: A narrow-task robot moving into a labor-short service trade is a counterpoint to general-purpose humanoid claims.

items.title: Vesoma exits stealth in Munich with 60-person team and Vesoma 1 humanoid
items.summary: Vesoma, founded in December 2025 by Synapticon co-founder Nikolai Ensslen and Easybrain co-founder Peter Skoromnyi, emerged from stealth with more than 60 staff in Munich and Limassol. Chief AI Officer Martin Riedmiller previously led research at Google DeepMind. It targets manufacturing, logistics and warehousing with a robot that learns from its own interaction. No funding or investors were disclosed.
items.why_it_matters: A European humanoid entrant with DeepMind lineage; the EU side of the comparison is otherwise thin.

items.title: O-ID raises $1.2M pre-seed for modular humanoid in Tokyo
items.summary: Tokyo-based O-ID raised $1.2 million in pre-seed funding led by TAWANI Ventures, with Hustle Fund, Techstars and angels, to move a modular humanoid for industrial manufacturing and logistics into production.
items.why_it_matters: Small Japanese entrant; low signal on its own, useful for the Japan column.
items.note_source: Source page failed a TLS check; details come from a search summary.

items.title: Kingfa robotics lead says most PEEK use in humanoids is hype; 6-10 kg of plastics per robot
items.summary: A Kingfa Tech robotics manager told Gasgoo that most current PEEK applications in embodied AI are hype, with PEEK priced up to about 1,000 yuan per kg. He put plastic content at 6-10 kg per humanoid, said 80-90% of material solutions are customised, and that about 400 Chinese firms are involved with only a handful above 1,000 units a year. Barclays separately flagged 26,000 tons of new Chinese PEEK capacity starting to ramp next year.
items.why_it_matters: A Chinese materials supplier tempering demand forecasts is a useful check on volume projections for the humanoid supply chain.

items.title: Mecka AI reported near a Sequoia-led round at about $500M valuation for robot training data
items.summary: TechCrunch reports Mecka AI, which pays people to record everyday tasks with body sensors and phones to train robots, is nearing a Sequoia-led round at roughly a $500 million valuation, three months after a $60 million round led by Framework Ventures. Round size was not stated and the deal had not closed.
items.why_it_matters: Human-motion data collection is becoming a funded layer of the robot stack, echoing other egocentric-video efforts tracked here.
items.note_dedup: Dated Sept 11, just before the window.

items.title: South Korea's science ministry outlines 2027 robot AI program starting with postal and logistics trials
items.summary: At Humanoids Summit Seoul, a Ministry of Science and ICT team head described a program starting in 2027 combining robot foundation and world models, a physical-data library and field trials in postal and logistics work. The budget is not finalised and should not be equated with the earlier KRW 2.3 trillion plan through 2030. Officials referred to a three-year window for competitiveness.
items.why_it_matters: It adds a third government program to the US-China comparison, with data collection treated as public infrastructure.

items.title: Unitree launches Dex5-S 22-DoF robot hand from $6,500
items.summary: Unitree announced the Dex5-S, a human-sized robot hand with 22 degrees of freedom and backdrivable joints, priced at $6,500 internationally before tax and shipping, or 39,900 yuan in China. Weight, grip force, tactile sensing and delivery schedule were not stated in the material reviewed.
items.why_it_matters: A list price for a dexterous hand sets a cost reference for a component US makers also build in-house.

items.title: Beijing E-Town sets Oct 17-18 Robot Warrior Challenge with 24 teams and 14 rescue and inspection tasks
items.summary: Beijing E-Town will hold a fall robot challenge on Oct 17-18 with 24 registered teams in six categories covering humanoids, quadrupeds and wheeled-legged robots, in remote-operated and autonomous classes. Tasks include door opening and valve closure. Top teams may get access to municipal inspection and security sites for field testing, per Global Times.
items.why_it_matters: Local government events tie robot testing to municipal use cases, a form of state-directed demand.

items.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 assets found in Tesla Android app; public reveal reported delayed
items.summary: Optimus Gen 3 renders reportedly appeared in Tesla Android app builds from late August, with higher-resolution versions around Sept 5. Trade reports say Musk pushed the Gen 3 reveal back, with Tesla focused on an Oct 1 Roadster reveal. Tesla has not announced Fremont Optimus output. Sourced to fan and trade sites, not Tesla.
items.why_it_matters: Tesla's stated Optimus timeline continues to slip while XPeng shows a line-built unit.

policy_ideas: FCC Covered List for foreign-produced advanced robots (July 28): FCC DA 26-957 (Sept 9) announced conditional approvals for certain routers and robots; track the Department of War conditional-approval list and the 65% US-sourced-component waiver test already recorded.

FY2027 NDAA conference: whether House Sec. 163 (humanoids), Senate Sec. 5813 (UGVs) and Sec. 847 (drone components including batteries, motors, controllers) survive; also the ASRA and GUARD language possibly riding along.

Pending bills to watch: Humanoid ROBOT Act (S.3275), National Commission on Robotics Act (H.R.7334), American Security Robotics Act (H.R.8189), GUARD Act (H.R.9129, adds humanoid and quadruped robots to the FCC Covered List).

Section 232 robotics and industrial machinery investigation (opened Sept 2025; 270-day statutory window elapsed): no proclamation found in this sweep; check Federal Register and BIS for a decision or a delay notice.

China rare-earth licensing: the October 2025 measures are suspended only until Nov 10, 2026, and US defense sourcing rules extend NdFeB magnet restrictions from Jan 1, 2027; both dates bear on actuator supply.
Chinese IPO gatekeeping for humanoid makers (report only, unconfirmed): watch CSRC/SSE/HKEX statements on valuation review, AgiBot's Hong Kong process, Leju and DEEP Robotics applications.

Standards: ISO 25785-1 (dynamically stable industrial mobile robots) remains a draft; final publication expected late 2026 or 2027. OSHA relies on the General Duty Clause plus ISO 10218 and ANSI/A3 R15.06-2025.
Korea: 2027 robot AI program budget not finalised; earlier KRW 2.3 trillion plan targets 1,000 humanoids a year from 2029 and 250 government-purchased humanoids in 2027.
Labor angle: reported Hyundai union position that no robot deploys without labor-management agreement (Seoul Economic Daily opinion piece; not verified against a primary source).
